takeaway: Vertigo on turning in bed with a positive Hallpike manoeuvre is benign positional paroxysmal vertigo (BPPV), from loose crystals in the inner ear.

question.text: A 38-year-old woman has a month of vertigo, severe when she turns over in bed; Hallpike is positive. What is the cause?
question.say: A 38-year-old woman has a month of vertigo, severe when she turns over in bed. The Hallpike manoeuvre confirms the diagnosis. What is the cause?

answer.say: Benign positional paroxysmal vertigo, B P P V.

lines.text: Our patient gets short attacks of vertigo whenever she turns in bed.
Inside the inner ear, calcified particles have been dislodged.
These loose crystals drift in the canal when the head moves.
It can follow head trauma or chronic otitis media, or arise spontaneously.
The Hallpike manoeuvre turns the head quickly, with the head held below the couch.
That reproduces the symptoms and confirms B P P V.
